REQUIRED UNDERSTANDING WHAT WE EXPECT YOU TO UNDERSTAND Power requirements - Electrical loads of mechanical plant · Single and three phase · Full load amps · Starting currents · Power factor Supply and distribution - Mechanical switchboards · Distribution boards · Sub-mains · Isolators · Circuit protection · Cable sizing principles Scope split - What the mechanical contractor supplies and installs · What the electrical contractor supplies and installs · Who terminates · Who commissions Controls interface - Control wiring · Field devices · Interlocks · Fire trip and shutdown signals · BMS interface points Motor control - Starters · Variable speed drives · Motor control centres · Control panels Essential services - Smoke exhaust and stairwell pressurisation electrical requirements · Fire mode operation · Emergency power interfaces Compliance - Relevant Australian Standards for the electrical interface · NCC requirements affecting mechanical plant WHY THIS MATTERS You will be expected to read a mechanical specification and an electrical specification together, and tell us what has been left out of both.

The stronger a candidate is across the areas below, the more highly they will be regarded — there is no upper limit here. The more accurate and the more confidently you can do them, the better. Outside air requirements - Correct outside air and ventilation rate calculations to the relevant Australian Standards and the NCC. Air conditioning selections - Confident AC selections across a wide range of project sizes and system types.

Fan selections - Correct fan selections — exhaust, supply, relief, smoke and car park — against duty and static. All equipment selections AHUs, FCUs, condensers, pumps, and all associated mechanical plant, selected accurately and commercially. PROJECT RANGE Our projects typically range from around $10,000 to $5,000,000.

We want someone comfortable performing accurate heat loads, outside air calculations and equipment selections across that entire range — from small works through to major commercial jobs. CONTROLS, BMS AND ELECTRICAL DEPTH Depth in controls and the mechanical / electrical interface is one of the strongest differentiators for this role.

The more genuine controls and electrical knowledge a candidate brings, the more highly they will be regarded. DEPTH WE REWARD Control logic - Understanding and writing practical control logic — how a system should actually sequence and respond. Controls understanding - Genuine understanding of controls philosophy, not just naming components.

BMS connections - Different BMS connection types, protocols and integration points. Controllers - Familiarity with different controllers and control hardware across manufacturers. Controls / mechanical / electrical crossover - The more a candidate can join up controls, mechanical and electrical thinking, the more valuable they are to us.

HOW THIS IS WEIGHTED These are not pass/fail requirements. They are a scale. Strength in accurate calculations, equipment selection, control logic, BMS and the electrical interface will lift a candidate above others — the deeper the genuine capability, the higher the regard.

FINDING GAPS AND VALUE ENGINEERING This is the part of the role we care about most, and the part that separates a good candidate from an exceptional one. Consulting engineers' tender documents are rarely complete or perfectly coordinated.

There are almost always gaps, ambiguities, missing scope, over-specified items and better ways to do the same job for less. We want someone who hunts for these instinctively — not because they are told to, but because they find it genuinely satisfying.

The right person treats every tender package as a puzzle to be picked apart, and every job as an opportunity to deliver the same outcome for less cost. This mindset directly protects and improves the margin on our work, and it is central to how the client competes and wins.

WHAT WE EXPECT YOU TO DO FOCUS IN PRACTICE Hunt for gaps at tender stage Read the consultant's drawings and specification critically. Find missing scope, conflicts, ambiguity and undefined responsibility before the price goes out — not after award. Challenge the documentation - Do not accept a consultant's design at face value.

Question it, test it, and raise RFIs where it is unclear, inconsistent or incomplete. Drive value engineering - Actively look for ways to deliver the same performance for less — alternative equipment, simpler routes, smarter staging, better procurement.

Find cost savings across the job - Look for savings throughout the life of the job, not only at tender: supplier haggling, drafting and engineering efficiency, labour reduction, warehouse stock, cranage optimisation.

Advise the estimators - Proactively flag to our estimators where you see cost savings, uplift opportunities or commercial risk while reviewing tender documents. You are their technical eyes on the job.

Turn gaps into position - Convert what you find into RFIs, qualifications, exclusions, variations and value-engineering proposals that protect and improve our margin.

THE MINDSET WE ARE HIRING FOR We want someone who opens a set of consultant's tender documents and feels excited, not overwhelmed — because they know that is exactly where the opportunities are hiding. If finding the gap and engineering the saving is the part of the job you enjoy most, this is the role for you.

Debar designs and manufactures bifold door hardware and complete bifold door systems for customers in the UK and international markets. While the principal focus will be existing products, the role will also contribute to larger product improvements and new development projects according to business priorities and team capacity.
Our products integrate precision mechanical hardware with aluminium profiles, requiring strong mechanical design judgement and an understanding of how changes can affect the performance of the wider bifold door system.

Product Sustaining, Improvement & Engineering Change
Take technical design ownership of engineering issues and improvements relating to Debar's existing bifold hardware, systems and wider released product portfolio.
Investigate product failures, recurring issues, customer complaints and warranty matters, developing robust engineering solutions and corrective product improvements where required.
Redesign components and assemblies where required to improve performance, reliability, durability or cost.
Assess the wider impact of proposed changes on mating components, aluminium profiles and overall system performance.
Carry out tolerance analysis and tolerance stack-ups where required to resolve fit, function or performance issues.
Lead the engineering content of product change requests, ensuring changes are properly assessed, documented and progressed through Debar's engineering change process.
Create and update 3D CAD models, assemblies, manufacturing drawings, specifications and Bills of Materials associated with product changes.
Own and maintain the technical content of documentation for released products, including end-user, fabrication and installation manuals, technical bulletins and supporting product information.
Maintain accurate technical product data and configurations within relevant industry software, including Logikal, ensuring that approved profiles, hardware, rules and product changes are correctly reflected.
Support product changes arising from supplier changes, material changes, component availability, obsolescence or alternative manufacturing requirements.
Identify and progress opportunities for proactive product improvement and value engineering.
Testing, Technical Issues & Collaboration
Work collaboratively with Debar's Compliance & Testing function to support testing or validation required as a result of product changes.
Support prototype components, trials and validation activity where required.
Liaise with customers, system partners and internal commercial teams on technical issues relating to existing products, investigating concerns and developing appropriate engineering solutions.
Work with suppliers on technical issues, alternative components, tooling changes and manufacturing feasibility.
Communicate the technical implications of product changes clearly to relevant internal and external stakeholders.
Product Development Support

Support new product and system development projects according to business priorities and Technical Engineering resource requirements.
Work collaboratively with Product Development engineers on projects requiring shared expertise or additional capacity.

Strong capability in parametric 3D CAD and manufacturing-ready engineering drawings.
